observations.observation: A producer-local layout winner need not minimize the producer-to-consumer edge; boundary conversion, direct consumer-native emission and zero-copy stride access must be compared as complete edge strategies.
observations.why_important: Without an edge oracle, a producer optimization can make the composed subgraph slower and cannot distinguish direct HND emission from NHD plus a hidden transpose.
observations.solution_decision: Enumerate legal NN, NH-copy, HH-native, HN-copy and view strategies; select by measured edge cost and retain a negative no-conversion region.
observations.experiment: v10 Stage0-3, five process repetitions, paired bootstrap CI and max(1%,3CV) threshold

observations.observation: Persistent cache/backend/layout commitment and live kernel adaptivity are different decision layers; a good local heuristic cannot recover alternatives removed by the persistent control plane.
observations.why_important: The solution must be hierarchical: preserve framework local experts while allowing a persistent policy to see batch, KV length, GQA ratio, reuse and system state.
observations.solution_decision: Use a persistent configuration selector plus local backend/kernel expert rather than replacing local heuristics.
observations.experiment: head-local versus token-local layout ranking across real attention shapes; v10 edge inversion is the stricter sub-test

observations.observation: The profitable layout scope is neither always global nor always per-operator: split domains win only when weighted consumer regret exceeds conversion, memory, fragmentation and pool overhead.
observations.why_important: An optimizer biased toward one global layout misses heterogeneous groups, while unconditional splitting loses in low-heterogeneity regimes.
observations.solution_decision: Search global, group/phase-specific and repaired split candidates under a hard memory budget; keep low-heterogeneity negative controls.
observations.experiment: directly timed common-NHD/common-HND/split-NHD+HND pipelines across multiple shapes

observations.observation: Layout conversion is a one-time investment whose break-even depends on future reuse/fanout and memory pressure; it must be paid once and shared, not charged independently to every consumer.
observations.why_important: Conversion-blind selection rejects profitable native-consumer layouts, while conversion-always policies waste bandwidth and cache capacity on short-lived tensors.
observations.solution_decision: Model conversion, temporary bytes and remaining reads jointly; admit view, materialize-once, producer-native and no-conversion candidates.
observations.experiment: conversion_reuse_pipeline at reuse 1/4/16/64 plus v10 H1.2/H1.3/H1.4

observations.observation: The relevant objective is token critical path or maximum rank time, not isolated attention latency; HBM, copy engines, TP/EP/All2All and overlap can reverse a local layout winner.
observations.why_important: A locally faster kernel can lengthen the system critical path by competing with communication or replicating KV state.
observations.solution_decision: Feed contention, placement and max-rank time into the layout objective; treat isolated timing only as a feature/baseline.
observations.experiment: isolated decode versus concurrent HBM-pressure decode; distributed TP/EP remains a required multi-GPU extension

observations.observation: Independent target/draft or producer/consumer choices can have an empty direct layout intersection even when a second-best pair, conversion edge or separate pool is feasible and faster than disabling the feature.
observations.why_important: Pairwise compatibility is not enough: metadata placement, page geometry, dtype and lifetime are part of the joint contract.
observations.solution_decision: Jointly enumerate consumer pairs and bounded repairs; compare common layout, repaired split and feature-disable baselines.
observations.experiment: multi-consumer common/split pipeline plus typed empty-intersection repair; native speculative decoding is external validity

observations.observation: Layout selection is a stateful control problem: the winner changes across workload regimes, but migration, graph recapture and replanning costs make per-request switching unstable.
observations.why_important: A static policy accumulates drift regret, while an aggressive policy thrashes; the missing variable is expected regime duration/remaining reads.
observations.solution_decision: Use epochal reconfiguration with hysteresis and measured migration cost, retaining a fixed policy for stationary traffic.
observations.experiment: measured primitive cost trace comparing fixed, per-request and hysteretic epoch policies

observations.observation: Shape and stride do not fully specify a layout boundary; axes, dtype, packing, scale format, page geometry, metadata placement, lifetime and device ownership form a typed edge contract.
observations.why_important: Without the full contract, a solver can choose physically plausible but semantically illegal layouts or miss a legal zero-copy/materialized repair.
observations.solution_decision: Represent accepted producer/consumer contracts explicitly, intersect them before costing, then attach legal repair edges.
observations.experiment: typed contract exact search, empty-intersection cases and all-subgraph boundary stride sweep

observations.observation: Fusion, tiling, pass order and layout selection are non-commutative: changing order changes both legality and performance, so layout cannot be optimized after a fixed fusion schedule.
observations.why_important: Sequential passes can permanently remove the fused/native-layout candidate that would have won globally.
observations.solution_decision: Generate semantic fused/order/layout candidates, prune illegal states first, and cost the remaining partial orders jointly.
observations.experiment: RoPE-before-convert, convert-before-RoPE and fused native-HND pipelines with correctness checking

observations.observation: Framework heuristics are useful local experts but their thresholds are not portable across shape, GPU, backend version and graph context; the learnable problem is residual selection among legal experts, not layout generation from scratch.
observations.why_important: A single static threshold overfits one regime, while discarding mature local experts expands the search space and loses legality knowledge.
observations.solution_decision: Use held-out shape/hardware evaluation for a residual meta-policy over framework candidates and report regret against an exhaustive legal oracle.
observations.experiment: best global static layout versus per-shape/per-consumer oracle; cross-GPU held-out run is mandatory for portability

observations.observation: A failed direct match is not proof that an optimization is impossible: algebraic rewrites, transpose/pack, producer-side emission and resource repairs can restore legality, but must obey memory and correctness bounds.
observations.why_important: Reject/fallback-only systems discard profitable neighborhoods; unrestricted repair can instead violate memory or silently change semantics.
observations.solution_decision: Run legality-first shortest-path repair search with explicit temporary/persistent bytes and retain reject/fallback as a candidate.
observations.experiment: empty direct intersection, illegal/over-budget repair pruning, and measured transpose repair cost
